# The Great GEO Measurement Crisis: Why Traditional SEO Metrics Are Failing in the Age of AI Overviews

## Introduction

We are in the middle of a seismic shift in how people search, discover, and consume information online. Traditional search engine optimization (SEO) grew up in an environment where the prize was clicks: organic traffic, pageviews, and conversion paths that started in search and ended on a brand’s site. Those KPIs have been the lingua franca of search marketers for a decade. But that world is changing fast. Generative AI features—AI Overviews, knowledge summaries, and conversational answers—are increasingly satisfying user intent directly on the results page. The outcome: fewer clicks, fewer measurable visits, and an urgent measurement crisis for anyone who still relies on legacy SEO metrics.

This post takes a trend-analysis view aimed at the generative engine optimisation (GEO) audience. We’ll map the trajectory of the problem, explain the mechanics driving it, present the hard data behind the shift, and translate those findings into practical tactics for content, analytics, and organizational KPIs. You’ll get the full picture: from the headline numbers that show how traffic is collapsing for some publishers to the more nuanced findings that complicate the simple “AI Overviews = zero clicks” narrative. We’ll also provide actionable takeaways you can implement now to stabilize visibility, measure impact, and evolve your SEO programs for a generative search-first world.

If you’re responsible for organic performance, analytics, or content strategy, this is the central trend you cannot ignore: nearly every established metric you depend on—organic sessions, CTR, goal completions attributed to search—needs to be rethought. The sooner you accept that the search ecosystem has changed, the faster you can shift to metrics and methods that actually reflect how users engage with generative results. Read on to understand why traditional SEO metrics are failing, and how to adapt with GEO-centric measurement.

## Understanding the GEO Measurement Crisis

At the heart of the GEO Measurement Crisis is a simple behavioral change: search engines are increasingly answering queries directly, and users are often satisfied without clicking through to a site. The mechanisms vary—AI Overviews that synthesize multiple sources, featured snippets, knowledge panels, and voice-activated answers—but the result is the same: a growing portion of search interactions that never produce a click.

Hard numbers make that stark. One set of industry data shows news publishers’ organic visits fell from roughly 2.3 billion in mid-2024 to under 1.7 billion by May 2025. That’s a ~26% collapse in less than a year, tightly correlated with a surge in zero-click results for news searches that went from 56% to 69% in the same period. In broader consumer behavior stats, only 40.3% of Americans now click on search results—down from 44.2% the prior year—and approximately 65% of all searches end without any click. Google’s AI summaries show up in roughly 10% of searches and handle an estimated 41 billion questions monthly. Other reports put the share of Google searches ending without a click at nearly 60%.

These are not edge cases. For mobile users, over 75% never make it past Google’s first page; combine that with AI Overviews placed above the organic results, and the share of clicks available to web pages shrinks dramatically. In extreme scenarios where AI Overviews dominate the SERP, some high-ranking pages report CTRs under 1%, versus the historical organic CTRs often above 15%.

The trend is more than a temporary experiment. Search engines are incentivized to show concise, trusted answers because user satisfaction and engagement metrics favor immediate answers. For Google and others that are deploying generative features, the value proposition is a faster, more conversational search experience. For brands and publishers whose revenue and reporting depend on pageviews, session counts, and last-click conversions, that evolution presents a measurement problem: how do you prove impact when the interaction you used to measure is disappearing?

To make measurement matters more complex, new research complicates blanket assumptions. A Semrush partnership with Datos studied over 200,000 keywords (volume > 100) between January and March 2025 to understand the effect of AI Overviews. They found that keywords triggering AI Overviews actually saw a slight decrease in zero-click rates—from 38.1% to 36.2%—during that window. That suggests the relationship between AI Overviews and clicks is nuanced: keywords that produce overviews tend to have informational intent and historically higher zero-click rates, so causation is not always clear-cut. In other words, the presence of an AI Overview sometimes correlates with high zero-click rates because of query intent, not simply because the overview exists.

Understanding the crisis requires holding two truths at once: (1) the aggregate data shows a clear decline in traditional click-based metrics and a rise in zero-click outcomes and AI answers; and (2) the impact varies by query type, vertical, and user intent. This dual perspective prevents simplistic conclusions and points to the need for sophisticated, multi-dimensional measurement frameworks.

## Key Components and Analysis

To adapt, you must understand the components driving behavior and how they interact. Here are the critical elements shaping the GEO Measurement Crisis—and what each one means for measurement and optimization.

- AI Overviews and generative summaries: These are concise, synthesized responses produced by the search engine’s generative models using multiple sources. They appear above or among organic results and often provide sufficient information to answer a user’s question, especially for informational queries. Because they satisfy intent without requiring navigation, they are the primary driver of zero-click outcomes in many verticals.

- Featured snippets, knowledge panels, and PAA: Traditional SERP features that predate generative AI already diverted clicks away from organic results. AI Overviews expand this effect by blending multiple sources and producing richer, more conversational answers, which further erodes click-through rates for organic links that previously benefited from user curiosity.

- Query intent and topic type: Informational queries—which often aim to get a quick fact, definition, or how-to—have always had higher zero-click tendencies. Retail or transactional queries still tend to produce clicks. The Semrush-Datos study showed that keywords causing AI Overviews often have inherently informational intent, which explains why they correlate with higher zero-click rates; causation is not automatic.

- Platform behavior (mobile vs. desktop): Mobile user behavior compounds the problem. More than 75% of mobile users never make it past page one, and the design of mobile SERPs gives even less space to organic results below generative answers. Voice and assistant-driven queries (which frequently rely on AI summaries) further reduce the click opportunity.

- Publisher impacts and revenue signals: For news publishers and ad-based models, the math is brutal. The cited drop from 2.3 billion to under 1.7 billion organic visits reflects both immediate revenue loss and longer-term devaluation of organic channels. When users don’t reach the site, ad impressions and subscription funnel interactions decline.

- Search engine strategies and public messaging: Google publicly claims a commitment to “sending traffic to the web,” with CEO Sundar Pichai quoted noting that Google prioritizes sending traffic to the web and projecting that “five years from now [we’ll be] sending a lot of traffic out to the web.” However, the current product trajectory of AI Overviews and summarization suggests a tension between promises and present outcomes, complicating baseline assumptions marketers used to make.

- Analytics and attribution breakdowns: Traditional last-click or session-based attribution fails when many interactions do not produce clicks. If an AI Overview answers a question and the user subsequently visits the brand through another channel, how should you credit that impression? Current models don’t capture the brand impact of being cited in an AI Overview or knowledge panel.

Putting these components together, the analysis is clear: the industry needs new metrics and a new measurement mindset. Impressions and rank are no longer the same as impact. Visibility on AI Overviews, branded mentions within generative answers, knowledge panel presence, and conversational snippet capture become as important (or more important) than organic visits.

## Practical Applications

So how do you act? Below are practical, tactical moves that GEO teams and SEO practitioners can apply immediately to mitigate risk and measure the new reality.

1. Optimize for generative outputs, not just links
   - Create concise, authoritative answers within pages that can be easily extracted into AI Overviews and featured snippets. Use direct question-and-answer blocks and clear summaries near the top of pages.
   - Incorporate schema and structured data aggressively. Schema helps search engines understand your content and increases the likelihood of being used as a source in an overview or knowledge panel.

2. Measure visibility instead of solely counting clicks
   - Track impressions across SERP features: featured snippets, PAA entries, knowledge panels, and AI citations. Use tools and APIs that surface SERP feature appearances. Visibility metrics will show your share of voice even when clicks are absent.
   - Build “AI mention” tracking: use exact-source monitoring to detect when your content is cited in generative answers and, when possible, log the context and phrasing.

3. Expand attribution models
   - Implement multi-touch attribution models that account for non-click interactions. Introduce “view-based” touchpoints: impressions in AI Overviews or knowledge panels should be assigned brand-lift value.
   - Use brand lift and aided recall studies to quantify the downstream value of being surfaced by AI summaries. Surveys that ask users about awareness after exposure can link visibility to conversion intent.

4. Prioritize content formats that survive generative extraction
   - Produce evergreen, authoritative guides structured with clear headings, short summaries, and fact boxes. Generative systems prefer such content for inclusion.
   - Create local-business-optimized pages with complete business info—GMB/Google Business Profile accuracy becomes vital because local answers often appear directly in SERPs and reduce site visits but increase local visibility.

5. Diversify traffic primitives
   - Lean into channels that are less dependent on search clicks: newsletters, direct subscriptions, social platforms, and app engagement. Use first-party data collection to reduce vulnerability.
   - Optimize for off-site conversions: payments, bookings, and subscriptions that can happen in-line or via structured result interactions.

6. Use experiments to measure downstream effects
   - Run A/B tests where you intentionally optimize some content for AI-readability and compare downstream metrics (brand searches, direct visits, conversions) against control pages. This helps establish causal links between visibility and business outcomes.

These applications are practical and immediate. They don’t rely on speculative long-term changes; they operate in today’s SERP ecosystem and prioritize capturing visibility and value where generative AI is already present.

## Challenges and Solutions

Implementing a GEO-first strategy is not painless. Expect resistance, tool gaps, and organizational hurdles. Below I lay out common challenges and concrete solutions.

Challenge: Attribution and analytics tooling are built for clicks
Solution: Extend analytics frameworks to accept non-click metrics. Use impression-level exports from Search Console and third-party platforms, tag SERP-feature visibility as events in your measurement layer, and feed those into your BI systems. If last-click persists as the budget lever, push for hybrid KPIs that combine click and view metrics.

Challenge: Revenue models tied to pageviews suffer when clicks evaporate
Solution: Re-evaluate monetization mixes. For ad-based publishers, negotiate API access or partnership models with search platforms where presence in AI Overviews or knowledge panels includes revenue-sharing or attribution credits. For subscription models, focus on direct acquisition channels (sign-up overlays, gated content) and use generative-optimized landing experiences to convert the smaller number of click-throughs at higher value.

Challenge: SEO teams lack skills for GEO/AEO optimization
Solution: Invest in cross-disciplinary training—NLP basics, schema implementation, and experiment design. Hire or train staff in “answer engineering”: crafting content specifically to be parsed into summaries. Treat this as a new domain of technical SEO.

Challenge: Organizational KPIs and incentives still reward volume, not visibility
Solution: Redefine KPIs to include visibility measures—featured snippet capture rate, AI mention share, knowledge panel appearances, and brand lift metrics. Realign compensation, reporting, and dashboards to reward these modern indicators.

Challenge: Interpretational ambiguity—correlation vs causation (Semrush-Datos nuance)
Solution: Do your own experiments and longitudinal analyses. The Semrush-Datos study found keywords with AI Overviews had slight decreases in zero-click rates during one quarter, showing that simple narratives mislead. Test across your verticals to identify where AI Overviews hurt clicks and where they don’t. Segment by intent, device, and query complexity to get actionable patterns.

Challenge: Risk of being deprioritized by platforms despite public commitments
Solution: Maintain diversified acquisition strategies and lobby via industry associations for transparency. Track platform product changes closely and adapt quickly—contract external partnerships for policy monitoring if needed.

These challenges are surmountable, but they require active investment and a willingness to change measurement and incentive systems. The organizations that move first will set the benchmarks and benefit from early leadership in GEO.

## Future Outlook

Looking ahead, several plausible scenarios and trends will shape GEO and measurement. Understanding these will help you plan a resilient strategy.

Scenario 1 — Hybrid equilibrium: Search engines stabilize a hybrid model where AI Overviews complement direct links for complex queries but send traffic for transactional intents. In this scenario, clicks decline but not uniformly; the winners will be sites optimized for being used as trusted sources in generative answers. Measurement settles on blended metrics: impressions + conversions + brand lift.

Scenario 2 — Generative-first dominance: AI Overviews and conversational answers become the default for many queries. Clicks plunge further, and visibility metrics, brand trust, and API-level partnerships become the primary levers for publishers. Platforms may create monetization pathways for high-quality sources that fuel their models.

Scenario 3 — Regulatory and partnership shifts: Public scrutiny or regulatory action forces platforms to disclose sources and provide better attribution, or to compensate original content creators. That could restore some traffic or create new revenue models tied to being cited in AI summaries.

Operational trends to watch:
- Measurement tool evolution: Expect analytics vendors to introduce AI-specific modules—AI mention detection, generative answer tracking, and impression-based attribution connectors.
- Content engineering: “Answer-first” content engineering will become mainstream. Writers will be trained to craft extractable answers and metadata that generative models can use.
- Increased importance of authority signals: Trust metrics (citations, publishing pedigree, author credentials) will matter more because generative engines prioritize trusted sources when synthesizing answers.
- Market consolidation: Enterprises that can invest in advanced tooling and data will get a disproportionate advantage capturing AI visibility. Smaller players will need to specialize or partner to stay competitive.

For forward-looking teams, the opportunity is to lead the formation of GEO best practices and to define the new KPIs that matter to executives. This is not merely a tactical problem; it’s a strategic redefinition of what search success looks like.

## Conclusion

The Great GEO Measurement Crisis is not a short-term hiccup; it’s a structural change in the digital information economy. AI Overviews and generative answers are rewriting the rules of search distribution, eroding clicks, and exposing the weaknesses of legacy SEO measurement. But this disruption also opens an opportunity: the organizations that rethink visibility, build measurement systems that value impressions and mentions, and optimize specifically for generative consumption will gain the new high ground in search.

Key facts to carry forward: news publishers saw organic visits fall from roughly 2.3 billion to under 1.7 billion within a year as zero-click news searches rose from 56% to 69%; some pages now see CTRs below 1% when AI Overviews dominate; roughly 65% of searches may end without a click, with about 60% of Google searches now zero-click; Google’s AI summaries appear in about 10% of searches and handle an estimated 41 billion questions monthly; yet nuanced studies such as the Semrush-Datos analysis of 200,000+ keywords show that the relationship between AI Overviews and clicks is complex and sometimes counterintuitive.

Actionable takeaways:
- Track visibility, not just clicks: log SERP features, AI mentions, and featured snippet share.
- Optimize for extraction: concise answers, structured data, and authoritative content increase the chance of being used in generative summaries.
- Evolve attribution: integrate impression-based and brand-lift measures into conversion models.
- Diversify acquisition and revenue: reduce dependence on pageviews by building direct channels and alternative monetization.
- Experiment and segment: run controlled tests to understand where generative features help or hurt your specific content.

The future of search is generative. Your measurement approach must catch up. Adopt GEO principles, update KPIs, and design your analytics to capture the value that no longer shows as a click. That’s how you weather the crisis—and turn it into an advantage.
